input.summary:
Church belfry (room-12) furnished: barrel of ringing supplies at (53,16,10) with a standing lantern on its top at (53,17,10) beside the bell; (53,16,11) and the ladder column x 52 stay clear. make.sh writes a whole build.nbt, belfry line shows 2 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
In a scratch copy with the belfry deck, ladder and bell added (test-belfry.mjs), the room check gives WALK ok (1 of 1 floor cells reached from the hole), LIGHT min 13 with 0 dark cells, and the only FIT note is a bell 'floating' flag on the scratch bell.
The look (room.png, from above) reads as a barrel with a lantern under the hung bell; nothing over a doorway or window.
left: Verified only in a scratch copy: in this copy shell-b (tower deck y15, ladder, bell at (52,17,10)) is still a stub, so the real merged room check (WALK/LIGHT) must be re-run once shell-b lands; the scratch harness adds those pieces.

Only one walkable floor cell exists in this 2x2 stage ((53,16,11)): the bell takes the head room over (52,16,10) and the ladder foot sits under (52,16,11). Any future furniture must keep (53,16,11) and its head room clear.

The room check flags the bell as 'floating' (air under it) even with the y18 deck above and attachment ceiling. Probably a checker false positive for hung bells; the tower builder or the tool owner should confirm.
Scratch files left in the part directory: test-belfry.mjs, rooms-test.json, test.nbt, room.png. Not part of the build; delete them when the merged room check replaces them.

waste.what: Placed furniture by rows in layers() but mis-indexed the first row as z 11 instead of z 10, so the barrel landed in the wrong cell, found only after a make and a room check.
waste.tool: A dry run for layers() that prints the drawn grid with its world coordinates (or a `mcd room --dry` on the drawing) before writing, so row order is checked before any build.

waste.what: The belfry's floor deck, ladder and bell belong to shell-b, which is a stub in this copy, so the room check had nothing to walk. Wrote a scratch harness to add them by hand.
waste.cost: one scratch script (about 15 lines), 2 rooms-test.json variants, and a walk-entrance trial (the entrance must be a standable cell outside the room)
waste.tool: `mcd room --with-shell <spec>` or a `--assume-shell` flag that adds the parts' planned floors, ladders and hung items from plan.md, so an interior designer can check the walk and light before the shell part lands.

waste.what: Walk-to-the-room and light trials were done by hand with different entrance cells and furniture placements to learn how the tool counts floor and headroom under a ladder hole and a hung bell.
waste.tool: `mcd room` output that says why a cell is not a floor (no support, head blocked by what, ladder foot), instead of the bare 'x' or ' '.

structured_output.summary:
Church belfry (room-12) furnished: barrel of ringing supplies at (53,16,10) with a standing lantern on its top at (53,17,10) beside the bell; (53,16,11) and the ladder column x 52 stay clear. make.sh writes a whole build.nbt, belfry line shows 2 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
In a scratch copy with the belfry deck, ladder and bell added (test-belfry.mjs), the room check gives WALK ok (1 of 1 floor cells reached from the hole), LIGHT min 13 with 0 dark cells, and the only FIT note is a bell 'floating' flag on the scratch bell.
The look (room.png, from above) reads as a barrel with a lantern under the hung bell; nothing over a doorway or window.
left: Verified only in a scratch copy: in this copy shell-b (tower deck y15, ladder, bell at (52,17,10)) is still a stub, so the real merged room check (WALK/LIGHT) must be re-run once shell-b lands; the scratch harness adds those pieces.

Only one walkable floor cell exists in this 2x2 stage ((53,16,11)): the bell takes the head room over (52,16,10) and the ladder foot sits under (52,16,11). Any future furniture must keep (53,16,11) and its head room clear.

The room check flags the bell as 'floating' (air under it) even with the y18 deck above and attachment ceiling. Probably a checker false positive for hung bells; the tower builder or the tool owner should confirm.
Scratch files left in the part directory: test-belfry.mjs, rooms-test.json, test.nbt, room.png. Not part of the build; delete them when the merged room check replaces them.

waste.what: Placed furniture by rows in layers() but mis-indexed the first row as z 11 instead of z 10, so the barrel landed in the wrong cell, found only after a make and a room check.
waste.tool: A dry run for layers() that prints the drawn grid with its world coordinates (or a `mcd room --dry` on the drawing) before writing, so row order is checked before any build.

waste.what: The belfry's floor deck, ladder and bell belong to shell-b, which is a stub in this copy, so the room check had nothing to walk. Wrote a scratch harness to add them by hand.
waste.cost: one scratch script (about 15 lines), 2 rooms-test.json variants, and a walk-entrance trial (the entrance must be a standable cell outside the room)
waste.tool: `mcd room --with-shell <spec>` or a `--assume-shell` flag that adds the parts' planned floors, ladders and hung items from plan.md, so an interior designer can check the walk and light before the shell part lands.

waste.what: Walk-to-the-room and light trials were done by hand with different entrance cells and furniture placements to learn how the tool counts floor and headroom under a ladder hole and a hung bell.
waste.tool: `mcd room` output that says why a cell is not a floor (no support, head blocked by what, ladder foot), instead of the bare 'x' or ' '.
